<div class="learn-box">
**What you will learn**

Install the client, choose a practice environment, and check both package versions.
</div>

This chapter creates the public synthetic GiBleed practice connection.
Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed
with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

## Before you start

You need R 4.1 or newer (the recorded run used R 4.6.2), internet access for
installation, and either an Opal with dsOMOP 2.10.4 or the local DSLite practice
server below. RStudio is a convenient editor; ordinary R also works. Download the book helpers below; you do not need a Git checkout.

Run this **installation block once**, before the examples. It installs every
package used by the lessons, the offline server and the reproduction tools.
Installation changes your library and is not executed during the book build.
The two dsOMOP tags must be available on GitHub; this book's recorded run used
the matching locally tagged sources.

```r
install.packages(c("remotes", "DSI", "DSOpal", "DSLite", "DBI", "RSQLite",
                   "resourcer", "withr", "openssl", "jsonlite", "knitr",
                   "rmarkdown", "pkgdown", "bslib", "opalr", "duckdb"))
remotes::install_github("datashield/dsBase@6.3.5", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("datashield/dsBaseClient@6.3.5", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("isglobal-brge/dsOMOP@2.10.4", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("isglobal-brge/dsOMOPClient@2.10.4", upgrade = "never")
```

The *client* is the package on your computer. The *server* runs requests near the
data; DSLite lets you run it locally for practice. Pandoc is also needed to rebuild
the site (RStudio includes it). The [reproduction notes](book-09-reproduce.html)
record the dependency versions used for this book.

## Get the book helpers

The released 2.10.4 package archive does **not** contain `tools/book/`.
Download [book-helpers.zip](../downloads/book-helpers.zip) from this site, leaving
it zipped in your Downloads folder. In R, run this block and select that ZIP
when the file chooser opens:

```r
book_dir <- path.expand("~/book-work")
dir.create(book_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
unzip(file.choose(), exdir = book_dir)
setwd(book_dir)
stopifnot(all(file.exists(file.path("tools/book",
  c("practice.R", "fixture.R", "connection.R", "display.R", "load-practice.R", "load-numeric.R")))),
  file.exists("tools/dates/va-native.R"))
getwd()
```

The last line prints your home directory followed by `/book-work`. In every new
R session run `setwd(path.expand("~/book-work"))` before the chapter setup.
The ZIP preserves `tools/book/` and `tools/dates/` automatically. Alternatively, save the individual
[practice](../downloads/practice.R), [fixture](../downloads/fixture.R),
[connection](../downloads/connection.R), [display](../downloads/display.R) and
[practice loader](../downloads/load-practice.R) and
[numeric loader](../downloads/load-numeric.R) files under `book-work/tools/book/`.
Keep the numeric loader filename `load-numeric.R`; the practice loader sources it.
Also create `book-work/tools/dates/` and save the
[released capstone helper](../downloads/va-native.R) there as `va-native.R`;
chapter 14's solution uses it.

`connection.R` is the one place to select DSLite or Opal and set the Opal URL,
project, profile and two resource names. Leave its defaults for local practice.

## Check the client


``` r
library(dsOMOPClient)
vapply(c("dsOMOPClient", "dsOMOP", "DSI", "DSLite", "dsBaseClient"),
       function(package) as.character(packageVersion(package)), character(1))
```

```
#> dsOMOPClient       dsOMOP          DSI       DSLite dsBaseClient 
#>     "2.10.4"     "2.10.4"      "1.8.0"      "1.5.0"      "6.3.5"
```

``` r
ds.omop.client.version()
```

```
#> [1] "2.10.4"
```

This reports the package on your computer. A correct client version alone does not
prove that the server has the matching methods.

## Load two public synthetic datasets

The practice server has two resources. **GiBleed** supports the introductory
schema and vocabulary lessons. **Synthea27Nj** supplies hemoglobin and other
numeric measurements with units for [Working with lab values](book-15-labs.html). Both contain fictional patients; “numeric”
means populated numeric fields, not real patient records. GiBleed has 44,053
measurement rows but no populated `value_as_number`, so it cannot teach lab-value
reducers on its own.

The administrator loader is [tools/book/load-practice.R](../downloads/load-practice.R).
It downloads pinned [Eunomia datasets](https://github.com/OHDSI/EunomiaDatasets),
verifies archive checksums and loads two SQLite files. For Synthea it calls the
[numeric validation loader](../downloads/load-numeric.R) unchanged, then copies its
typed DuckDB tables into portable SQLite, checking all 39 row counts. Dates retain
ISO calendar text and numeric values retain numeric types. The temporary DuckDB
copy is removed. This adds the `duckdb` package to the installation block above. From your `book-work` R session, run the loader once:

```r
system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"),
        c("tools/book/load-practice.R", "../practice-data"))
stopifnot(file.exists("../practice-data/gibleed.sqlite"),
          file.exists("../practice-data/numeric.sqlite"))
```

It uses the installed DBI, RSQLite, duckdb, withr, openssl and jsonlite packages. The source data are Apache-2.0 licensed;
keep their [license](https://github.com/OHDSI/EunomiaDatasets/blob/3d349dcdd79cc346b8e36eb837e49feffe7f7497/LICENSE)
with redistributed copies. The recorded loader results are in the reproduction notes.

<div class="book-note">
**Note**

Chapters 5, 7, 9, 10 and 12–14 also use a tiny, separately labelled questionnaire
**test fixture** for the colleague's exact education, cause-of-death and partial-date
examples. Its 24 fictional people and invented question concepts are not GiBleed
or Synthea. It is created temporarily by `tools/book/fixture.R`, not installed as
a third practice resource. Each chapter states its dataset.
</div>

## Open the practice server

To reproduce without Opal, install the matching dsOMOP package and DSLite, DBI,
RSQLite, resourcer, withr, dsBase and dsBaseClient. Use `book-work` as your R working directory. DSLite executes real DataSHIELD methods inside R;
this helper creates one server with both loaded resources and attaches GiBleed.


``` r
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/connection.R")
source("tools/book/practice.R")
practice <- if (book_driver == "DSLite") book_practice("gibleed") else book_connect("gibleed")
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
```

```
#> [1] "site"
```

`conns` holds connections, not patient rows. The other resource is named `numeric`.
Every chapter includes its complete fresh-session setup, including assigning
`conns <- practice$conns`. Numeric chapters select `"numeric"` through the same
configuration. Questionnaire chapters source `fixture.R` and call
`practice <- book_fixture()` before assigning `conns`; this is always local DSLite.

## Check the server


``` r
ds.omop.server.version(conns = conns)
```

```
#>   server published running missing ready advice recipe_language
#> 1   site    2.10.4  2.10.4          TRUE           2, 2.0.0....
```

The reply comes from the server. Check both the installed and published versions
when using Opal: publishing makes the package methods available to analysts.

## Use the same two resources on Opal

**Optional administrator walkthrough; requires a Docker host.** Ordinary readers
can continue with DSLite. These deployment commands were checked against the
[easy-opal source](https://github.com/isglobal-brge/easy-opal/blob/main/src/services/rock.py)
and [opalr resource API](https://www.obiba.org/opalr/reference/opal.resource_create.html).
The book build tested both databases and all analyst chapters with DSLite.
**A live easy-opal deployment was not run for this revision: Docker was unavailable.**
The success lines below are acceptance criteria, not recorded Opal output.

### Start the practice stack and mount the databases

On the Docker host, install Docker with Compose V2, then install easy-opal. Obtain
the helper ZIP and load the two databases there exactly as above. The host layout
must be `~/book-work/tools/book/` and `~/practice-data/`. Run in a terminal:

```sh
uv tool install easy-opal
easy-opal instance create book
easy-opal -i book setup --stack-name book --host localhost --ssl-strategy none --http-port 8080 --yes
easy-opal -i book up
easy-opal -i book status
cd ~/book-work
bash tools/book/book-compose.sh up -d --force-recreate rock
bash tools/book/book-compose.sh exec -T rock sh -c 'test -r /data/practice/gibleed.sqlite && test -r /data/practice/numeric.sqlite'
```

Use `pipx install easy-opal` if you do not use uv. The setup prints the local
Opal URL and administrator password; keep them for the next step. This local
practice stack uses HTTP. For a remote deployment use your administrator's URL.
The shell helper uses the generated instance directory
`~/.easy-opal/instances/book`; if `easy-opal instance info book` shows another
location, set `BOOK_OPAL_INSTANCE_DIR` to it.

The ZIP includes this concrete Compose overlay, `tools/book/book-rock.yml`:

```yaml
services:
  rock:
    volumes:
      - type: bind
        source: ${BOOK_DATA_DIR}
        target: /data/practice
        read_only: true
```

`book-compose.sh` resolves the absolute host data directory and combines this
overlay with easy-opal's generated `docker-compose.yml`. The original Rock
`/srv` volume is retained. Use `bash tools/book/book-compose.sh up -d` and
`bash tools/book/book-compose.sh stop` to manage the mounted stack thereafter.
After an easy-opal configuration change, run `easy-opal -i book up`, then the
`--force-recreate rock` command above again to restore the overlay. Reapply the
package installation steps after recreating Rock if its image lacks the packages.

### Install in Rock and publish the DataSHIELD methods

First install the SQLite driver and GitHub installer **inside Rock**:

```sh
bash tools/book/book-compose.sh exec -T --user root rock Rscript -e 'install.packages(c("remotes", "RSQLite"), repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")'
```

In `tools/book/connection.R`, set `book_driver <- "Opal"`, set `opal_url` to the
URL printed by setup, and retain `opal_project <- "practice"`, the two default
resource names, and `opal_profile <- "default"`. These are the same settings all
public practice chapters read. In your local R environment set
`BOOK_OPAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD` to the generated password, `BOOK_OPAL_USER` to a new
analyst name (for example `bookreader`) and `BOOK_OPAL_PASSWORD` to its password.
Run `file.edit(path.expand("~/.Renviron"))` and add these lines, replacing the
placeholders with your values (retain quotes around passwords). This is a private
local file, not a shared notebook:

```text
BOOK_OPAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD="<password printed by easy-opal>"
BOOK_OPAL_USER=bookreader
BOOK_OPAL_PASSWORD="<choose a password of at least eight characters>"
```

Save the file and restart R so those environment variables are loaded.

From an R session in `book-work`, run:

```r
source("tools/book/opal-admin.R")
```

This downloadable [administrator script](../downloads/opal-admin.R) logs in as
`administrator` (or `BOOK_OPAL_ADMIN_USER`), installs dsBase 6.3.5 and dsOMOP 2.10.4
in the configured profile with `dsadmin.install_github_package()`, then calls
`dsadmin.publish_package()` for both. Publishing registers their assign/aggregate
methods and package options. It creates the named analyst if absent, grants
DataSHIELD and profile use, creates the project and these resources, and grants
the analyst resource `view` permission (the permission used for DataSHIELD).
It leaves disclosure thresholds unchanged and refuses an existing resource whose
URL or format differs. Existing analyst passwords are not reset.

| Configured resource | URL inside Rock | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `practice.gibleed` | `omop+dbi:sqlite:///data/practice/gibleed.sqlite` | `omop.dbi.db` |
| `practice.numeric` | `omop+dbi:sqlite:///data/practice/numeric.sqlite` | `omop.dbi.db` |

SQLite needs no database credentials. The script declares `package = "dsOMOP"`
on each resource so its resolver loads when assigned. It prints the installed
package versions and resource definitions for checking. In the Opal browser UI,
log in as the administrator using the same URL, open **Administration → DataSHIELD**,
and verify the selected profile lists dsBase 6.3.5 and dsOMOP 2.10.4 with published
methods. Resources remain database references; do not import them as downloadable
patient tables.

### First analyst login and checks for both resources

Keep only the analyst credentials for ordinary lessons. In a fresh R session:

```r
setwd(path.expand("~/book-work"))
source("tools/book/check-opal.R")
```

The [check script](../downloads/check-opal.R) uses the same configuration and
DSOpal login as the chapters, prints `site` and `ds.omop.server.version()`, then
attaches each resource and requests its measurement schema. Both calls must
return a nonempty schema before these success lines can print:

```text
PASS: practice.gibleed connected; measurement schema returned
PASS: practice.numeric connected; measurement schema returned
```

Confirm installed and published server versions are 2.10.4 in the version reply.
A failed login, missing driver, unpublished method, unreadable mount or wrong
resource name stops the checks; do not proceed to the lessons until both pass.
The script disconnects and logs out. Start the chapter's visible setup to log in
again. [Chapter 2](book-02-connect.html) exercises switching on the same connection.

To move to a future demo Opal, transfer the same two SQLite files to its Rock
mount, run the resource provisioning with that host's administrator, and update
only `connection.R`. No database TLS setting or study-specific privacy setting
is needed.

## Recap

You can distinguish your client installation from the server installation and have a practice connection.
